To overcome this hurdle, we present a new, fast, and compact node embedding method called Sparse Structure Preserving Node Embedding (SSNE), designed to improve the quality of node embeddings by preserving the intrinsic topological structure of the network. By utilizing the weighted random walk strategy, we ensure that the node embeddings produced by SSNE maintain the original graph's topology. Furthermore, we optimize the efficiency of node embedding production by breaking down the large, sparse network into smaller sub-networks and calculating the necessary statistics for embedding production. Our experiments on six real-world event networks demonstrate the superiority of SSNE over state-of-the-art node embedding methods in terms of node embedding quality and the accuracy of network link prediction methods that utilize these embeddings.

Highly advanced nano-fabrication techniques are utilized to produce small chambers made of silicon for use with atomic cesium, to aid in the development of a precise laser cooling and trapping laser micromirror. The silicon material is highly transparent to optical light due to the characteristics of silicon photonic crystal technology, which allows the design of small chambers to be easily produced. The material properties of silicon also enable the use of silicon micro-lenses and other optical components within the device, which can be fabricated at a highly precise level using silicon processing methods. The developed silicon chambers are among the most precise silicon photonic crystal devices produced so far, with the potential for use in various atomic physics experiments.

This study investigates distortion power in dual-polarization 4D-APQ and 4D-QPSK formats, examining the impact of modulation mapping schemes involving different phase and amplitude combinations. Four mapping schemes are analyzed: (a) unitary amplitude, (b) symmetric non-unitary amplitudes, and (c & d) asymmetric non-unitary amplitudes with constant symbols when mapped to the same spatial mode. The research compares the bit error rate performance between the unitary and non-unitary mapping schemes in fiber nonlinear channels, finding the unitary scheme to be more resilient to nonlinearities. The study also uses the stepwise noise power method to evaluate and optimize the symmetric and asymmetric mappings to achieve equivalent noise power and, ultimately, bit error rate.

We introduce the Fire-Invisible Reconstructing Generative Adversarial Network (FIRe-GAN), a cutting-edge deep learning-based model that leverages integration of visible and infrared images to create hyper-realistic images of wildfires. FIRe-GAN employs a unique generative approach, combining residual learning and spatial-temporal smoothing within the encoder, along with an advanced adversarial learning process that includes a specialized wildfire discriminator. Our model surpasses the current state-of-the-art techniques, providing hyper-realistic wildfire imagery capable of significantly enhancing visual fidelity. The FiRe-GAN source code can be accessed at https://github.com/AlperenYildirim/FIRe-GAN.

Detecting signs of depression on the internet is crucial for addressing the limitations of current mental health care systems. Social media analysis, when applied to identifying mental health issues, can be an effective tool. By examining online content, researchers can pinpoint crucial indicators, making it possible to develop early warning systems and provide prompt, accessible mental health care. In this study, we examined how a machine learning model trained on multiple social media platforms performed in identifying depression within Twitter posts, offering insights into utilizing social signals to address depression and proposing new platforms for further exploration.

This study presents and evaluates a stochastic, compartmental model that predicts the spread of COVID-19 within a population divided into distinct groups under varying confinement levels. We derive mean-coupled differential equations as an approximation of the model and investigate its associated stochastic dynamics. By analyzing the mean-coupled equations, we can derive a stable equilibrium state representing steady-state COVID-19 levels in the population under long-term confinement policies. We also derive inequalities bounding the mean number of infections within the population at any given point in time. A simulation study demonstrated that these bounds are effective in a wide range of scenarios and are tightly bound in certain conditions. Furthermore, we found that strict long-term confinement has negligible impact on population health outcomes. By comparing model outputs with COVID-19 data in Italy, bounding results were able to accurately predict the number of active infections a week ahead with high precision under certain policy conditions.

Our study utilizes the Gogny-Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov method combined with the quasiparticle-phonon model to investigate the Giant Monopole Resonance (GMR) in Mg-24 and Si-28. A notable aspect of this research is the coupling of isoscalar quadrupole states with the main GMR state, resulting in a secondary, lower-energy resonance. This phenomenon, observed in both Mg-24 and Si-28, is attributed to the strong interaction between these states, facilitated by a strong quadrupole-quadrupole interaction. A comparison with experimental data shows that our theoretical predictions align well with both energies and the full width at half maximum. Additionally, our model is able to replicate a small low-energy tail in the resonance, in agreement with experiments.

A study of the stick-slip phenomenon and the convergence of systems governed by Coulomb friction is conducted. This is achieved through the development of existence and uniqueness criteria under various velt fields. These conditions are applied to multiple scenarios, including step inputs, bounded inputs, and reguared feedback systems. This framework is further extended to systems incorporating friction-induced non-smoothness via the application of invariant separation techniques. This proof of convergence is then used to establish the stability of a hybrid controller designed for robotic grasp tasks.

Reinforcement learning faces significant challenges in handling nonstationary environments. The introduction of Off Policy Risk Management (OPRM) addresses this issue by decoupling the behavior policy from value assessment, thereby enabling risk-aware policy optimization. However, OP's reweighted importance sampling, crucial for correction, suffers from high variance, rendering it impractical for real-world use. This paper proposes the first application of Bellman risk decoupling, which mitigates the high variance issue and enables stationary policy risk optimization through a novel correction mechanism. The proposed method, R-Max-MAP, employs a single network to learn both an optimal and risk-adjusted policy, offering improved sample efficiency and interpretability. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of R-Max-MAP over other risk-aware methods in solving challenging risk management tasks, including real-world scenarios like robotic navigation, where it exhibits substantial sample efficiency gains.

Sequential recommender systems are pivotal to numerous online activities.
They anticipate the sequence of actions a user will take, given their past
behavior. Traditional sequential models primarily rely on memory-based or deep
learning methods that forecast future actions solely according to previous events,
resulting in recommendations centered around past behavior. To address this
shortcoming, we introduce the concept of user intent. A framework is developed
to extract user intent from past behavior, which is then leveraged to generate
intent-driven recommendations. The framework consists of a memory module to
retain user state and a neural encoder to capture latent user intent, modeled
using the Variational Autoencoder. The effectiveness of our proposed framework
is demonstrated through time-series recommendation evaluations on MinersDatasets.

The solvable double confluent Heun equation, with its parameter dependencies, is expressed through a series of transformations based on the parameter k, resulting in three key cases: k equals zero, one, and higher values beyond zero and one, leading to distinct forms of the equation in each instance. For k equals one, a specific case arises that encompasses a general unfolding of the double confluent Heun equation, characterized by symmetric properties in its potential. These findings not only confirm previously known conditions but also provide new, specific forms of the equation, opening up new avenues of research in this field.

Matrix-based data analysis is often hindered by the presence of groupwise heterogeneous vectors, and and a crucial question arises - which data aspects can be accurately assessed in the presence of these vectors? We have developed a comprehensive framework that addresses this issue from a fundamental perspective and provides insights into both data aspects and estimator characteristics. We have proven that a linear estimator achieves these bounds and demonstrates that a coherent, though non-linear, estimator performs comparably well under certain natural conditions for a broad class of group sizes. We have validated these findings through empirical tests.

Quantum systems exhibiting symmetry-protected topological properties are characterized by specific symmetry classifications and can be identified through characteristic boundary states that emerge from broken symmetry in low-dimensional environments.  A novel class of topological substances has been identified through machine learning, featuring an extraordinary resilience that persists even when symmetry-protection is removed.  This resilience is attributed to their inherent non-Abelian $\pi_1$-index, a topological characteristic that remains intact due to their energy gap's stability.  A prototype, known as the Chern insulator with chiral edge modes, has been created by engineering a gap that cannot be closed without a spatial dimension increase.  A chiral SIA model has also been developed, initially displaying symmetry-based protection but ultimately being found stable even after symmetry-protection is removed.  This discovery expands our understanding of topological substances and provides an avenue for further theoretical investigation and experimental validation.

The semi-inclusive Lepton Flavor Equivalence ratio, a novel observable derived from $b\to s\ell^+\ell^+$ processes, offers enhanced sensitivity to new physics effects and a superior stochastic property. Calculations of this ratio, along with the individual contributions from $B\to D^{(*)}\ell_1\ell_2$ and $B\to K^{(*)}\ell_1\ell_2$, are performed using partial cross sections. The resulting predictions for the semi-inclusive ratio, with significant sensitivity to the two non-vanishing Wilson coefficients, are compared to the exclusive ratio, and the former is shown to offer a more robust benchmark.

This paper presents a novel approach to designing distributed controllers for a class of linear systems that must maintain stability, robustness, and adaptability to changes in the network's topology, all with a fully decentralized architecture. The proposed regulation problem involves creating a distributed extended state estimator and a distributed dynamic compensator that can stabilize any connected network's extended state, regardless of its configuration. The proposed estimator and compensators are innovative as they can accommodate new agents to the network in real-time without the need for recalibration, thanks to their adaptive design that uses only local measurements and an upper bound on the network's size. The approach is validated through theoretical research and numerical simulations, demonstrating its ability to stabilize and robustly track signals in complex network topologies, all while maintaining robustness to changes in parameters and communication noise. The results also highlight the significant impact of parameter design on the robustness of the distributed system and the significant performance improvements that can be achieved with optimal tuning.

The COVID-19 outbreak is a major global event that has had far-reaching consequences on world politics, the economy, and social interactions. Its rapid spread is challenging healthcare systems and imposing severe financial burdens on governments. A unique characteristic of COVID-19 is its ability to initially spread quickly, followed by an unprecedented decline due to implemented containment measures. To address this complex situation, a novel machine learning approach combining BERT and Reinforcement Learning has been developed. This method's success relies on a novel technique called BERT-Split-Train, which utilizes the representation learning capability of BERT to split and train models into two interconnected phases: one focused on the rapid growth phase and the other on the implementation of control measures. By incorporating BERT's pre-trained knowledge and training models separately on distinct COVID-19 datasets, this approach offers a resilient solution capable of adapting to dynamic real-world scenarios.

Network research encompasses multiple disciplines, including computer networks, biological networks, and social networks. In recent years, researchers from all these areas have contributed significantly, expanding our knowledge of network structures and their properties, as well as developing various network characteristics and models. Our aim is to serve as researchers in the network space as navigators, providing a framework for exploring these diverse domains. We focus on bridging the gaps between these fields, emphasizing the importance of converging knowledge to advance network theory and application. By highlighting the network landscape, we seek to foster collaboration and innovation across network research and its subfields.

The intricate relationship between ecological and evolutionary processes is a complex interplay of temporal dynamics and controlling factors.  Understanding this interplay is complicated by various mechanisms that influence how fast ecosystems change, such as environmental heterogeneity, interconnectedness of populations, and selective pressures.  We have developed a set of theoretical tools to study the interplay between ecology and evolution under different regulatory mechanisms and varying environmental conditions.  We have identified two key timescales that determine whether ecosystems undergo rapid ecological changes or slower evolutionary processes, such as genetic adaptation and trait changes.  Our research reveals that certain mechanisms can shorten these timescales and facilitate faster evolutionary processes, while others can extend these timescales and lead to more complex eco-evolutionary dynamics.  We have also found that ancient ecosystems may have experienced different eco-evolutionary dynamics than those of today, suggesting that understanding these dynamics is crucial for uncovering the evolutionary history of species.

Characterizing how knowledge transfer generalizes and fails to do so is vital for
comprehending self-supervised speech learning, and it reveals the mechanisms
behind its success and its limitations. We scrutinized the transfer
antisusceptibility of a self-supervised speech learning model's Borsh, which
involves training on one audio dataset and then performing on a different one.
Using a speaker- and language-agnostic assessment, which involves training on a
single speaker and evaluating on another from an unseen speaker, we discovered
that Borsh exhibits significant antisusceptibility in a few acoustic and
automatic speech recognition tasks. Furthermore, we discovered that
antisusceptibility arises from two primary factors: inter-sample variation and
variation among samples within the same group of samples. Through analysis of
model antisusceptibility and the use of a teacher-student learning method, we
demonstrate that borsh's antisusceptibility performance can be surpassed. Our
findings have implications for understanding generalized learning and suggest
a potential direction for enhancing self-supervised learning models.

This study examines the potential of emerging distributed ledger technologies, with a focus on their ability to facilitate more decentralized, transparent, and efficient digital exchanges through distribution. We highlight the advantages of blockchain and its underlying protocols, such as cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and network architecture, which underpin trust in digital transactions and distributed exchanges. The research also explores the potential impact of blockchain technology on digital exchanges, drawing on a theoretical framework that integrates institutional theory, blockchain adoption models, and digital exchange knowledge. We developed a comprehensive model to assess the influence of blockchain-powered distribution on decentralized exchanges and identified key strategies for centralized exchanges to embrace distributed ledger technologies and successfully transition to decentralized models.

A widely accepted strategy for addressing missing data in Bayesian analysis involves using missing at random (MAR) as an assumption, despite the associated risk. To evaluate whether an analysis is robust against model specifications, it has become crucial to assess how well data sets conform to the MAR assumption. To this end, we explore the application of the E-value in measuring test robustness in order to quantify the extent of missingness unexplained by known covariates. Our investigation demonstrates that under a Bayesian framework with linear regression and normal models, the validity of missing data imputation methods analogous to those used for observed data can be guaranteed.

The quantum affine algebra $U_q(\hat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ has multiple finite-dimensional modules that are isomorphic up to a twist. These natural modules have been utilized to develop two distinct approaches for the quantum plane $\mathbb{C}_q[x,y]$. Although $\mathbb{C}_q[x,y]$ is not a based Hopf algebra, it does possess a limited set of Hopf algebra automorphisms. Furthermore, we identify the complete set of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ symmetries in the form of rational and Laurent modules, and we establish their structure within the endomorphism Hopf algebra of $\mathbb{C}_q[y]$.

The ever-connected vehicle has become a cornerstone of the intelligent transportation systems.  One of the major challenges in modern vehicle applications is the efficient sharing and processing of data. Federated learning has emerged as a viable solution, but current approaches face difficulties in verifying the security of the training process.  A novel framework leveraging blockchain technology has garnered significant attention in overcoming these limitations.  A comprehensive review of existing literature has been conducted to identify research gaps in this area.  This paper provides an in-depth analysis of recent advancements in FL for smart vehicle applications using blockchain, highlighting its benefits and challenges.  Furthermore, it explores potential opportunities for future research in this area.

Measurements of charged hadric jets associated with D mesons and prompt jets are presented for proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV. The data corresponding to rapidity intervals between 1.5 and 2.5 and 2 and 4, with an invariant mass between 25 and 45 GeV for one jet and between 20 and 45 GeV for the other, have been collected using the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The observed ratios of events containing D mesons to those containing prompt jets across all measured intervals deviate significantly from the predictions of the C++-Lund model at the low end of the jet transverse momentum spectrum. The observed differences are attributed to non-perturbative QCD effects.

The Fermilab Quantum Information Center - National Institute of Standards and Technology Collaboration (FQC-NISTC) has developed an advanced platform for quantum information processing that operates at extremely low temperatures, specifically millikelvin. This cutting-edge facility is built within an underground bunker at Fermilab, leveraging the benefits of the site's proximity to a state-of-the-art helium-3 refrigerator, along with access to expert-level technical expertise and access to quantum and superconducting computing technologies. This platform spans approximately 1,500 square feet and houses multiple quantum computing platforms, incorporating a unique combination of quantum sensors, entangled photon sources, and tailored optical tables. By harnessing these technologies within a highly controlled environment, the Fermilab-NISTC collaboration aims to advance quantum information processing at a national level, utilizing the benefits of a research facility operated by a prominent quantum computing research institution.

This research paper explores misuses of the Bitcoin protocol encountered in the cryptocurrency space. As the cryptocurrency market continues to expand, a significant number of projects adopt Bitcoin, adopting parts of the protocol to build their applications. However, a substantial percentage are found to be non-compliant with the full protocol, a phenomenon that has been dubbed the 'Bitcoin Comply or Perish' (BoCP) phenomenon. A recent study revealed that 68.2% of cryptocurrency projects on the Ethereum Virtual Machine do not adhere to the standard ERC-20 token protocol. Similarly, our study demonstrates that approximately 70% of software using the Bitcoin protocol do not comply with its specifications, a phenomenon that shares similarities with the BoCP phenomenon, thus revealing another instance of this prevalent issue.

Automatically labeling map elements in geospatial data has been a major challenge for years, with traditional methods relying on online polls from drivers. However, these methods are limited by the low response rates online surveys typically yield. A new approach called WORTH was developed to enhance driver-based geospatial data collection by increasing poll participation and providing real-time driver feedback. By utilizing this optimized process, researchers successfully gathered over 150,000 answers within a single year in a single metropolitan area. To achieve this, they analyzed various factors affecting participation rates, identified the optimal poll presentation timing, and implemented various measures to engage drivers. Furthermore, experiments revealed that participants' responses were accurate and contained little regional bias. A real-time system was also created to enable drivers to view their contributions in a meaningful way, demonstrating that people are more inclined to contribute when they understand the impact of their actions.

Seismic reflection sparse modeling has become a widely accepted approach for the effective recovery of reflectivity, but it is often limited by its inability to accurately represent nonuniform sparse signals due to its assumption of uniform sparsity. While sparsity is crucial, its uneven distribution across frequencies and time periods significantly impacts reconstruction quality, with higher frequencies typically being sparsely represented. This work proposes a novel proximal mean network, a deep learning model, that captures nonuniform sparsity patterns and their influence on reconstruction. The model is formulated as a proximal gradient descent algorithm, with the proximal operator learned using the network and the subgradient of the nonuniform regularizer computed analytically. This framework is versatile and can be applied to a variety of sparse reconstruction problems by adjusting the nonuniform regularizer and its influence level.

Our investigation centers around the characteristics of operator semigroups within various forms of BMOA-like spaces, with a particular focus on how these spaces interact with Ma's operator T_n and the Looman-Bernstein operator L_n. We establish that when n is greater than or equal to 2, the canonical semigroup of operators associated with T_n does not preserve the structure of the modified BMOA space, denoted as BMOA^log, nor does the Looman-Bernstein operator L_n possess a semigroup of operator representation for any n greater than or equal to 2 in BMOA^log, a conclusion that we also support with numerous concrete examples involving a wider array of BMOA-like space categories.

Within the context of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory, we investigate the behavior of wavefunctions, which are derived from wavefunction overlaps. These overlaps serve as correlation functions in the large central charge limit of two-dimensional conformal field theories. By examining the overlap of wavefunctions associated with circular spatial intervals, we establish a connection to the operator amalgamation overlap (OAO) framework developed by Guo, Liang, and Wen. This relationship enables us to uncover universal finite-size effects governing the entanglement entropy of disjoint intervals. Furthermore, we utilize the Haagerup model to demonstrate how OAO-based wavefunctions can be employed to calculate entanglement entropy in non-unitary modular tensor models.

Historical collections hold invaluable insights into past languages, yet their unique characteristics pose significant challenges for current NLP tools to utilize them effectively. We developed a new framework to predict part-of-speech (POS) tags from unannotated texts via machine learning. The task involves assigning a list of probable POS labels to each word in the text. We utilized feature-rich neural networks, specifically transformers, to extract text and POS context, and a time-series forecasting approach. The latter was used to generate a list of probable POS labels, along with confidence intervals, for each word. We tested our framework using 19th-century German corpora from three distinct domains. The results demonstrated that models with lower prediction variance were associated with higher corpus reliability in subsequent tasks. Moreover, manual inspection revealed that our model's higher-confidence predictions were generally accurate, while lower-confidence predictions often contained notable errors.

To handle non-smooth paths in non-conformal harmonic vector calculus, a comprehensive framework is developed and applied in the context of non-rearrangement problems. This includes a non-Schlomilch condition to ensure the integrability of composite functions at non-smooth points. Formulas are formulated for the non-conflict integrability of functions involving a non-conformal harmonic function and a non-smoothly differentiable vector-valued function, with a non-Schlomilch condition on the partial derivative. Furthermore, a non-conformal version of the Schlomilch condition is formulated for the partial derivative to guarantee the integrability of functions in the form $f_j(h(x),h'(x),\phi(x))$. This is expressed as $|\partial h(x)/\partial x_j|<\infty$ for non-rearrangement problems and is proven that the non-rearrangement condition and the non-Schlomilch condition are necessary for the integrability of composite functions. Formulas are also formulated for the non-conflict integrability of functions in the form $f_j(h(x),h'(x),\phi(x))$ with non-rearrangement conditions, and a non-conformal generalization of a non-rearrangement condition is presented for the partial derivative as $|\partial h(x)/\partial x_j|<1$, $j=1,2$. This is extended to the integrability of functions in the form $

A crucial phase in developing reliable software systems is converting a system's requirements into a formal specification.  However, this process is typically carried out by specialized engineers due to the complexity involved.  As smart city technologies continue to evolve, a city dweller may now express a desire to have their input reflected in formal specifications.  To address this issue, we've designed an intelligent assistant that enables the translation of ordinary language inputs into formal specifications.  This framework, based on the Expectation Specification Formalization Ontology (EFO), allows for flexible and adaptable specification of items, services, and behaviors within a city context.  A smart assistant has been developed to leverage knowledge represented in EFO, facilitating software reliability, safety, and accountability.  Furthermore, we'll demonstrate the practical application of proposed methods through a city expectation case study.

As a promising platform for building large-scale quantum computers, superconducting quantum systems are plagued by quantum error issues.
To overcome this problem, a strategy called the concealed inverses protocol utilizes gate error asymmetry to mitigate errors without relying on quantum error correction.
In this paper, we demonstrate a more effective implementation of the protocol, achieving greater benefits through optimized gate error asymmetry.
Leveraging superconducting quantum systems' inherent gate asymmetry, our improved procedure sets a new benchmark for the protocol's potential in these systems.
Specifically, our results show that $C_4$ and $C_8$ multi-qubit gates can experience error reductions by factors of 15 and 8, respectively.
This outcome significantly enhances quantum computational capabilities, particularly for algorithms requiring deep circuits, thereby facilitating large-scale quantum applications.

This research investigates the possibility of representing order relations in a category, specifically a regular one, by depicting them through a type of graph called a cospan. To do this, we first establish the necessary conditions for a category to have "pullbacks along maps," a property that is equivalent to being "extensively 2-extensible." With these foundations laid out, we then explore various applications and implications, including the ability to depict maps with "extensive properties" and the depictions of natural transformations in categories that are "extensively 2-complete." Furthermore, we also examine whether certain categories, like the one formed by all ordered sets and monotonic functions, can be represented in a categoryistic framework, and explore a method for testing equivalence of preorders through depictions in a category, leading to a categorization of "extensively 2-complete" categories based on a particular property.

Spatial extreme weather events can be analyzed by examining the conditional peak of a multi-dimensional geographic area, which takes into account the observed extreme weather at a particular monitoring station. This study involves analyzing the conditional peaks of four English marinas to understand the extreme weather patterns under specific climatic conditions. By utilizing the Gaussian copula, the team is able to identify the conditions that lead to the most severe extreme weather patterns in these locations. This study also highlights the effect of extreme weather on marina environments and how it can be influenced by geographical and environmental factors.

State-of-the-art vision-language models like VT-CLIP excel at generalizing visual understanding across various domains, primarily due to their ability to capture semantic connections between visual and textual information through contrastive learning. Nonetheless, these models tend to overly rely on textual embeddings and fall short in focusing on detailed visual representations. To address this issue, we introduce a multi-task learning framework centered on visual guidance. Our approach involves combining two key tasks: predicting textual descriptions corresponding to images and generating images matching textual inputs. By doing so, we enhance the capability of a pre-trained visual encoder to learn nuanced visual features and connect them with a text encoder via a shared visual-language projection module. To further refine the projections, we employ a two-stage contrastive learning strategy. Experimental results across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the substantial performance gains achieved by our model over current state-of-the-art approaches.

A matrix-valued system evolves over time, represented by a linear operator acting on a complex, multidimensional vector space, which can be extremely large and highly abstract in some applications like quantum chromodynamics and superconductor networks. Utilizing a relatively low-dimensional effective representation to simulate these systems can be computationally advantageous due to their linear nature, which allows for the efficient handling of large matrices and operators. In this context, a novel approach called operator switching is proposed for managing noisy matrix evolutions, which can be computationally beneficial when dealing with high-dimensional linear dynamical systems. By representing the operator as a superposition of a small set of basis operators and periodically switching between them, based on a predetermined schedule, operator switching can reduce the dimensionality of the matrix evolution, enabling the efficient simulation of certain systems, such as those involving non-Abelian anyons and quantum spin systems. Numerical experiments demonstrate that operator switching can result in a substantial speedup over conventional matrix-evolution methods when simulating a one-dimensional Ising chain in a magnetic gradient at equilibrium.

We identify the $k$-th homotopy group of the $k$-th Postnikov stage of quaternionic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra with integer coefficients, specifically $\tau_{\le k} H\mathbb{H} \simeq \tau_{\le k} \mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{H})_ {20|20p} for 20 \le k \le 39$.

In a p-1-regular local ring R, a compact Hilbert polynomial polynomial P(n) of large degree d, with d less than or equal to e, results in a module of nilpotent derivations D_n(R) possessing the property of being F-nilpotent. This is contingent upon R having a characteristic p≥3.

The number of model results being generated for scientific research and clinical use cases is growing rapidly. Standardizing exchange formats for model evaluation and visualization is crucial for effective communication between developers and end-users. However, current formats have limitations, particularly in providing enough information for reproducibility and clinical applicability. This work proposes Highdicom, a Python framework for standardizing high-level results, including segmentation and classification outputs, according to the DICOM standard. Highdicom emphasizes the optimization of existing standards over creating new ones and accommodates various model types and training procedures. It also offers Python tools to generate and validate Highdicom-compliant data and includes comprehensive metrics and a clinical report template. Highdicom currently supports standardized metrics for prominent imaging tasks and includes examples of valid reports for pathology and radiology.

A detailed analysis of the Einstein-Hilbert action's surface expression reveals that its associated Noether charge can be broken down into specific components. One part of this decomposition corresponds to the holographic counterterm method's contribution to the Schwarzschild entropy, while another relates to a central charge within the Virasoro algebra. By examining the subtractions made to regularize the Noether charge, we can derive the relationship between the entropy of black holes and the Virasoro entropy, ultimately demonstrating the equivalence of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy expressions derived from different approaches.

In recent years, deep learning has gained significant traction in processing DNA sequences. However, the heavy reliance on manually designed features and the high computational requirements of deep models have led to questions about the necessity of these approaches. In response, a novel, fully unsupervised embedding learning framework called DNAEmbed has been developed to learn DNA sequence embeddings without relying on pre-existing biological knowledge. By using DNAEmbed, we can eliminate the need for feature engineering and achieve competitive results on various DNA classification tasks such as gene prediction, promoter identification, and functional element classification. Additionally, our analysis of the learned embeddings reveals that they effectively capture various levels of DNA sequence information, offering new insights into biological understanding.

The interaction between surfaces or interfaces can significantly alter the electronic properties of a material. To explore these modifications, researchers have utilized the technique of molecular beam epitaxy to grow an ultrathin metal-insulator film, specifically V$_2$O$_3$, on a single crystal sapphire substrate. To investigate how surface properties impact metal-insulator behavior, they further modified the film with vanadium oxide molecules. Their results showed that the film could no longer switch between its two distinct states when modified, revealing an interesting transition between two metallic-like states. Through the use of advanced spectroscopy, researchers discovered that the film's electronic structure undergoes significant changes due to these modifications, revealing a fascinating connection between structural and electronic properties at the surface level.

The application of the Clebsch technique to reduce Lie-Poisson systems yields novel Hamiltonian structures with potential practical benefits, where it involves transforming Lie-Poisson frameworks into a different Lie-Poisson structure and two Hamiltonian terms, one of which has the reverse characteristics.

Exoplanet research has recently focused primarily on planet candidates that are located in areas of the sky that are closely monitored. Our team, however, has successfully identified 22 new prime field candidates and an entire new star system in 2018 by meticulously examining all available data from the Southern Prime Field. Additionally, we discovered 12 additional candidates in the Southern Prime Field that were not published, and a total of 12 new candidates in the Southern Prime Field. In order to achieve this, we employed machine learning to rapidly filter out false positives and manually verified the remaining candidates. Our findings demonstrate that the Southern Prime Field continues to be an excellent source of valuable exoplanet discoveries.

We have developed a novel method for achieving second-order spatial accuracy in numerical simulations of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations, employing a novel approach to enforce physical principle adherence at all times. By integrating FVCA-2 on unstructured triangular meshes within a finite volume framework, we have successfully maintained adherence to entropy and kinetic energy positivity. Extensive testing through various benchmark tests has validated our approach. Notably, our method exhibits robustness under extreme conditions, allowing for high-resolution simulations with fine mesh structures, thereby enabling detailed and precise numerical calculations. Furthermore, our approach successfully captures intricate flow phenomena, such as shock cells, shock-vortex interactions, and boundary layer transitions, as demonstrated in our extensive test suite.

The evaluation of algorithms from Multiple Classifier Systems was conducted,
using 5 algorithms on a dataset from an Indian bank, which tracks clients
over 10 years to assess their borrowing behavior. This analysis involved
tracking the clients' changes from year to year, thereby transforming the
issue into an Multi-Label Multi-Task Learning challenge. Two feature
selection techniques were employed - based on statistical methods and machine
learning - to uncover essential clients for year-to-year transitions.

A simultaneous application of two approaches, q-rooth theory and the study of Dyck paths, led to the development of two polynomials. One polynomial, associated with the symmetric group Sn, encodes the distributions of specific involution statistics, while its counterpart, associated with Sn-2, is linked to the type B Stanley symmetric functions. This second polynomial was found to be equivalent to the elementary symmetric functions, with coefficients representing the sum of certain involution statistics appearing in type B Demazure characters. Furthermore, these coefficients were shown to possess the unimodal and unimodal-log-concave properties. Utilizing an inductive framework, the presence of the Pascal Riemann matrix was also demonstrated.

Deep learning models have achieved significant success in vision tasks, notably image classification. A key factor influencing their performance is the architecture, which dictates the flow of information and influences model behavior. In this research, we investigate the impact of input data on orientation within convolutional neural networks. By incorporating explicit orientation information, we developed two new input layers, providing the network with orientation information through separate channels. Our findings indicate that providing the network with explicit orientation information enhances its performance by enabling the detection of orientation-invariant features.

Building on previous research by the author, where a new trace equation was developed for the group PSL$_2$(ℤ), under a curvature assumption, this note extends that work to a broader class of groups involving matrices with entries from a finitely generated monoid. Specifically, a novel equation for the relative trace of the indicator function representing the set of matrices with a given degree of length is introduced. This equation relates to the relative trace of the set of matrices containing exactly one non-negative matrix, due to the curvature assumption. We demonstrate that under the curvature assumption, the curved linear interval condition holds, thereby deriving the trace equation for the curvature-dependent group class in question.

A substantial, flavor-dependent top quark weight ambiguity, reaching 5-10 GeV, may originate from the QCD evolution of nonperturbative hadronic matrix elements associated with local heavy quark operators at the boundary of heavy quark effective theory. This significant top quark weight uncertainty surpasses the current precision of its momentum space counterpart, as demonstrated by recent experiments. The investigation explores the feasibility of reducing this top quark weight ambiguity through strategies like employing low-scale effective theories or low-momentum perturbation theory.

Our subset of vertex edges to continuous coloring in a specific group of graphs is based on an established theorem, which states that for large enough values of $k$, such graphs can be edge-colored in a specific way, where every group of $k$ vertices has edges that can be colored with a specific set of values. We aim to expand the applicability of this result by further investigating the conditions under which this theorem can be applied to a broader range of graphs. We establish a new condition, showing that for large enough values of $k$, such graphs can be edge-colored in a specific way, where every group of $k$ vertices has edges that can be colored with a specific set of values. We also provide additional examples and counterexamples to illustrate the applicability of our result.

We establish a form of hypercontractivity for weighted $L^p$ spaces of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^d$, incorporating arbitrary parameters. We also confirm the nonexistence of bounded contraction operators from the $L^2$ class to the $L^3$ class within scaled Bergman spaces.

A highly contagious and deadly form of pneumonia called COVID-19 has become a global pandemic, with a COVID-19 Computer Tomography (CT) scan being a reliable diagnostic tool. Although high-dose images can identify COVID-19, they risk harming patients due to excessive radiation exposure, prompting the need for a low-dose detection method. To this end, a novel two-stage Time-distributed Capsule Network, incorporating a Squeeze-and-Excitation module, has been developed to detect COVID-19 in low-dose CT images at a level of accuracy comparable to that of a human doctor without expert labeling. This model was successfully tested on the latest established low-dose COVID-19 dataset, known as CheXplain, with encouraging detection results.

This study focuses on organizing space resources into a hierarchical and interconnected 3D system that is divided into distinct regions, allowing for a more detailed understanding of how these resources interact with one another. By utilizing a grid-based approach, we can accurately map out the movement of celestial objects and identify areas where space can be utilized most efficiently. Our methodology involves analyzing the movement of objects using a specific mathematical framework, known as the Hill-Clohessy-Wiltshire equations, to gain insight into their behavior and interactions within this space. By incorporating a flexible framework that can be adjusted as needed, we can gain a more comprehensive understanding of how space is utilized in different regions of the universe, while also taking into account the movement of objects over time. Our analysis reveals that a specific type of space organization, known as Radial Equatorial (REO), exhibits unique characteristics that make it particularly well-suited for studying complex systems and their behavior. By extending our findings to include a more comprehensive framework, our study contributes to the broader understanding of how space is utilized in different regions of the universe, paving the way for future research into the behavior of these complex systems.

Creating unstructured high-quality 2D meshes on complex 3D parts from Catalogue of Part Models (CPM) is challenging due to their varied shapes and sizes. This work presents a novel approach called Q-Mesh, designed to automatically generate order-highest quads mesh on any part. The process initially involves creating a coarse mesh, followed by a finer mesh through triangle splitting. The innovation of Q-Mesh lies in its unique solution to the initial step where it solves a whole number linear optimization problem, unlike traditional approaches, to create an order-highest quad mesh. Comprehensive testing on multiple models demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

We're exploring methods to obtain exact analytical expressions for understanding the behavior of sample correlation coefficients when different datasets are uniquely arranged, with applications in evaluating properties of dependent rank arrangements in a two-way sample space. This investigation focuses particularly on correlational aspects of comonotonic and anti-comonotonic dataset pairs in the 2-adapted two-way sample space, with dependency structures rooted in the binomial distribution. We've found that setting specific parameters in a general formula yields accurate mean and variance expressions for sample correlation in both anti-comonotonic and comonotonic dataset pair scenarios. This investigation also examines comonotonic dataset pair dependency structures arising from a uniform distribution model, with the aim of providing precise expressions for expected mean and variance of sample correlation.

This review outlines the application of the S-matrix approach to scattering amplitudes in general relativity and theories more complex than it. We focus on tree-level amplitudes and utilize various mathematical tools, including spinor helicity, gauge invariance, and soft limits, to derive and derive compact expressions for scattering processes. Key outcomes include deriving compact expressions for tree-level n-point amplitudes in gravity and exploring the double-copy structure connecting gravity and gauge theories. Additionally, we examine how these amplitude techniques can be applied to the study of black hole dynamics and other gravitational phenomena.

This paper presents a novel finite-dimensional interior feedback control scheme for stabilizing solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in three dimensions. The control mechanism is designed to stabilize solutions within specific Sobolev and Besov space ranges, and it's demonstrated that low-dimensional control is sufficient to achieve this across various critical space ranges. The proof relies on the robustness of the Navier-Stokes equation with respect to external forces under the Banach fixed point theorem, and the control strategy is shown to be optimal at dimension.

Language learning can be greatly facilitated by well-designed web-based dictionaries that provide intuitive navigation and a wide range of features. WDL, a large dictionary for the Lithuanian language, boasts nearly 1.5 million word entries. This study introduces D3, a user-friendly web dictionary, and presents a plan to merge it with L1D3, another dictionary, to boost the quality of linguistic data within Lithuania.

A key aspect of deploying machine learning models in society is their explainability, which is particularly significant for AI recommendations. Current approaches to providing explanations for these models often lack transparency, particularly in the recommendation domain where numerous items are presented simultaneously to users. LIME, an existing explanation method, has been adapted for this purpose but is restricted to a single user-item pair, whereas in practice, personalized recommendations involve presenting multiple items to a single user. We introduce LIME-RS, a novel extension of LIME, which can generate explanations for multiple items per user, and we establish a new standard for evaluation by defining two key criteria: compliance with the model's predictions and the stability of explanations. LIME-RS parameters are optimized to maximize compliance, and our results show that, despite being limited to two predicted positive labels per item, LIME-RS can still generate high-quality explanations that are more accurate than any other method.

Quantum wells near the band edge of a semiconductor superlattice often encounter the issue of Fermi level level fixation at the barrier states due to doping, which significantly impacts carrier properties and cannot be ignored in numerical simulations, yet remains poorly understood experimentally. Our study investigates the physiological factors affecting Fermi level level fixation in an undoped quantum well system composed of Ga$_{0.51}$In$_{0.49}$ barriers and InAs layers. To mitigate this phenomenon, we developed a specific growth technique that increases interlayer distances between the well and barrier interface states, allowing us to experimentally verify a reduction in Fermi level level fixation. Our research also outlines practical strategies for minimizing or controlling this effect in quantum engineering applications.

In the context of non-iid data, our research investigates the performance differences between regional and random query distributions. We have created a mixed data model that explains how performance varies depending on the level of data overlap between clients. When the overlap is low, we show that a data aggregation model with client subsampling, which gives more weight to infrequent clients, outperforms traditional models like FL-PRD and KFE, which treat all clients equally. We have also experimentally verified that our proposed model is more effective than FL-PRD and KFE in simulated non-iid learning scenarios.

We propose a precise and efficient algorithm for computing the optimal transport matrix, known as Rapid Sinkhorn, with the guarantee of machine precise accuracy. By introducing the $\mathcal{K}$-matrix, our approach achieves numerical exactness, and by leveraging the structure of the $\mathcal{K}$-matrix, we develop an algorithmic improvement that converges in linear time for sub-exponentially regular distributions. In two dimensions, we find that the $\mathcal{K}(\sigma_\rho \times \sigma_\rho)$ matrix possesses a distinct collinear triangular arrangement, and by optimizing the storage and storage of the non-zero elements, we present a memory-efficient algorithmic solution. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive empirical evaluation of the algorithm's performance on various regular and sub-exponentially regular distributions, demonstrating that it can reach machine precise convergence in linear time.

The flaring activity of AU Mic, a young K5 dwarf, has been linked to the significant atmospheric erosion of its close-in planets, AU Mic b and c. This study investigates the connection between AU Mic's behavior in extreme ultraviolet light and other spectral ranges by comparing its FUV activity levels with those from other spectral ranges, including X-rays, XRT observations, optical flare events, and coronal mass ejections. During our FUV observations, we found that AU Mic's behavior is similar to its XRT behavior, with the star mostly in a dormant state, occasionally experiencing large flare eruptions. These flares and coronal mass ejections are comparable in magnitude to those seen in other young stars with active coronal mass ejections, such as AB Dor. Our findings suggest that extreme UV emissions from AU Mic could be significantly higher than predicted by its FUV levels, potentially leading to significant energy losses for its close-in planets. Consequently, these findings have significant implications for atmospheric erosion models of AU Mic b and c.

Lattice dynamics play a crucial role in determining the characteristics of electrons and other quasiparticles, but when an electron is highly energetic, it can interact with the lattice in a more complex manner, leading to the emission of phonons. A hypothesis has been proposed that this rapid movement of an electron causes it to drag the surrounding lattice, and in solid substances, this process could be observed through a distinct pattern of sound waves. This theory, known as radiation response drag, suggests that the movement of an electron is accompanied by a phonon wake, and in this paper, we explore this concept by examining how it affects electrons in both isotropic and directionally arranged lattices. We also investigate the interaction between the electron and the surrounding lattice in a model that considers the movement of atoms as a continuous medium.

In the realm of data analysis, the distinction between balanced and unbalanced, or unequal, datasets holds significant importance. Conventional machine learning algorithms typically assume balanced datasets, where every class has an equal number of samples. However, real-world data often exhibits disparities in class sizes. A standard approach to address this imbalance involves the k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) algorithm. Yet, traditional kNN is class-balanced, necessitating modifications for unequal datasets. This paper proposes a statistical method called Closest Neighbor on Unequal Data (COU), which redefines the classification criterion by incorporating statistical measures. The COU algorithm is then applied to two datasets, including the well-known Iris dataset, to showcase its effectiveness in handling unequal data.

We introduce a new sample of 1,582 quasars, including 288 highly luminous ($M_{UV} \geq -24.5$) quasars, identified through photometric data from SkyMapper combined with existing catalogs. The complete sky sample of 2,824 quasars, identified using machine learning, encompasses 1,234 newly discovered objects, making it the most comprehensive collection of high-redshift quasars ever identified. The majority of our newly discovered quasars, comprising 88% of the 288 extremely luminous objects, are located at distances greater than 1 Gpc. The combined dataset allows us to construct a refined luminosity function for quasars, revealing a notable deviation from previous models at extremely high brightness levels, primarily due to our discovery of numerous ($z > 1.5$) quasars with absolute magnitudes exceeding $-24.5$. The existence of this new population of extremely luminous quasars at high redshifts suggests that they may be the ancestors of the supermassive black holes residing in present-day nearby galaxies.

To study the charge-tunneling process in a quantum dot, we developed a new method using a quantum point contact as a detector. This approach, combined with superconducting materials, allows for precise real-time monitoring of charge fluctuations within the quantum dot as its energy levels are adjusted by gate electrodes. Our experiments, conducted at millikelvin temperatures with a proximized aluminum layer, demonstrate that electrostatic gating can induce stable tunneling of electrons and, more significantly, holes between the quantum dot and the superconducting domain. These results are supported by a theoretical model that accounts for various factors, including Kondo effect and excess hole behavior.

We examine the contraction properties in entropic variational inequalities for a broad class of preservation law systems, extending the contraction principles from non-entropic variational inequalities to entropic variational inequalities, which will be the focus of a future study. Our current work focuses on establishing the contraction properties for the entropic variational inequalities, taking into account the uncertainty in noise and initial data within a preservation set, which is crucial for assessing the accuracy of numerical solutions in low Mach number limits. To achieve this, we rely on a fundamental principle, which serves as a starting point for determining the entropy fluctuations in a preservation set, which is essential for obtaining the entropy inequality.

Current single-view 3D models primarily rely on a combination of sparse LiDAR data and images captured from mobile robots. Visual models focusing solely on images struggle to effectively utilize dense features captured by visual data, resulting in inconsistencies between captured images and geometric structures. In response to these limitations, we propose DiffDreamer, a novel neural approach that uses only a single view to reconstruct 3D environments. Our model effectively integrates optical flow and LiDAR data, employing a diffusion process that conditions 3D volume generation based on 22 steps of optical flow and one data point per scene. The generated 3D volume can then be combined with a single view to produce a highly detailed 360-degree view, surpassing traditional voxel-based methods and achieving reliable scene reconstruction on large-scale datasets.

The growing presence of networked systems in society necessitates predictive capabilities to manage and mitigate potential risks effectively.  Previous approaches focused on counterfactual forecasting, attempting to determine the effects of hypothetical interventions on a target network, often relying on a predetermined model.  However, these methods are inherently model-based and necessitate model parameter estimation, which can be a time-consuming and difficult task, especially for complex systems.  In an effort to overcome these challenges, a new framework has been developed that utilizes appis - a type of artificial data - to facilitate forecasting of desired outcomes on target networks without the need for explicit system modeling or parameter estimation.  The framework demonstrates impressive results in a simulation involving the spread of an epidemic across a complex disease-regulation system, showcasing its potential for efficient risk management in complex model-based systems.

Research into condensation and drying processes on and around cylindrical surfaces has gained significant attention. A recent experiment has been conducted to study the behavior of a thick liquid layer on a vertical fiber, observing the emergence of large-scale droplets through an instability that combines the effects of gravity and surface tension. Utilizing high-speed imaging, the study captured details of the instability's progression, observing the formation of rivulets and subsequent droplets. A theoretical model that accounts for liquid viscosity demonstrated that viscosity enhances droplet production by accelerating droplet separation.

This research explores the Lipschitz robustness of the Hunter-Saxton formula and its associated metric on the space of smooth functions, in relation to a given direction. We establish that the induced metric on hyperspheres of C^1 functions remains equivalent to the standard metric of the space, in the C^1 topology. We also consider modifications to the formula to ensure its compatibility in the weak* topology of BV functions, in the context of two-dimensional oriented surfaces.

Assessing scoliosis through ultrasonography can effectively identify the curvature's characteristics and aid in curvilinear angle measurement. Ultrasonic scanning along the spinal curvature's axis enables the detection of the maximum bend angle. Although scoliosis evaluation using ultrasound technology has been successfully implemented in a clinical environment, the process is highly reliant on operator skill, necessitating strategic placement of the transducer. In this research, we investigate whether there exists an optimal scanning strategy to enhance scoliosis evaluation reliability. We explore various strategies, including random and grid-based approaches, and compare them to the traditional manual method employed by a clinician. We evaluate and contrast the performance of these techniques by analyzing their impact on the curvilinear measurement error. Our experimental results demonstrate that a grid-based scanning strategy outperforms other methods in terms of curvilinear accuracy, with an average error of 1.29 degrees.

To enhance our text-to-speech system's performance, we've developed a text-independent approach that adjusts synthetic speech duration without needing analysis of the textual content. Our model leverages acoustic features to model duration through a non-statistical, linear strategy based on the median value. This strategy is characterized by its simplicity and the non-required text analysis, allowing for broad applicability across various text-to-speech platforms.

The growing prevalence of online hate speech poses a significant challenge to data and security systems.  Due to its vast and varied nature, hate speech detection through AI systems remains an ongoing area of research.  This study addresses the complex nature of hate speech by proposing a novel framework, incorporating a novel data embedding technique.  Experimental results demonstrate the proposed framework's effectiveness, with an outstanding performance, as evidenced by its state-of-the-art scores, achieving a precision of 0.99, recall of 0.98, and an F1-score of 0.98.

This research paper explores the potential of exchanging technical characteristics in advanced wireless communication systems. In particular, a novel technique is introduced to measure the effectiveness of MIMO channel mapping by utilizing low-resolution modulations. This approach aims to optimize high-gain MIMO channel performance mapping to a relatively simple modulation scheme. By demonstrating the practical feasibility of this technique with binary phase shift keying modulation, a significant improvement in MIMO communication capacity is observed and it is shown that a substantial enhancement can be achieved even with a modest number of antennas.

There are numerous digital archives of medieval manuscripts, but a significant challenge lies in their discovery due to the lack of comprehensive listings for many projects. Many of these collections are geographically dispersed across the internet, necessitating the use of specialized search strategies to locate them. Our review summarizes the main machine learning datasets used for manuscript minium identification, categorizes them by accessibility, and provides a detailed overview of the principal machine learning resources for manuscript identification, including their associated domains. We also introduce five new proposed datasets for the task and outline future directions for the research.

Robot joint performance is greatly influenced by flatness. To improve joint performance and minimize errors, an innovative approach has been developed that utilizes this concept in conjunction with feedback from additional sensors. This system monitors real-time error signals, which serve to refine model parameters. By implementing an adaptive adjustment mechanism, both the speed of convergence and stability of the control system can be optimized. To validate the effectiveness of this method, an experimental evaluation was conducted on an industrial robot, specifically a KUKA KR16 Robot.

A new approach for analyzing complex sequential data has been developed.  To study patients who have experienced a myocardial infarction, we have created diverse health states and used these to track their multidimensional health patterns over time.  This allows us to examine how various factors, such as age, sex, and socioeconomic status, influence these patients' life trajectories and identify potential pathways that may impact their survival and quality of life.  These states can also be used to create data models and identify areas for improvement in patient care and healthcare policy.  This approach has been successfully applied to a large cohort of patients with myocardial infarction, and our findings highlight the importance of adopting a holistic view of these patients to optimize their long-term health outcomes.

The concept of multi-site quadrature involves approximating functions with singularities in complex systems using precomputed values from a quadrature model. This approach has led to faster algorithms for key computational chemistry tasks involving singular integral equations. Multi-site quadrature can be applied to three-dimensional problems like continuum solvation integrals by initially calculating coefficients based on the Stokes operator in spherical geometry. This initial step can then be utilized at various atomic sites in large molecules or systems. A preliminary study showed that linear scaling computations for the implicit region in ab initio quantum chemistry can be achieved with this approach. This research demonstrates that multi-site quadrature can be highly accurate in molecular continuum calculations, particularly when handling atomic nuclei, by introducing an adaptive method for placing spherical radii and excluding overlapping radii. Employing spherical radii also facilitates the efficient computation of cross-terms, further accelerating implicit region calculations.

We explore the parameterized complexity of the metric dimension problem, focusing on specific graph classes and modifications. It's known that MD is efficiently solvable in certain graphs, but proving its NP-completeness for general graphs. This research extends previous findings by showing that even when parameterized by specific structural parameters - such as feedback vertex group, cycle basis size, or unimodular skeletal representation - MD remains an intractable problem. The novel proof techniques utilized in this study could potentially be applied to other problems in the field of parameterized complexity and graph theory.

A fundamental aspect of descriptive set theory is the identification of well-structured classes of spaces within various mathematical domains. For instance, a classical result by Lusin demonstrates that specific types of trees can generate numerous Polish spaces through a continuous mapping process, which can effectively categorize all such Polish spaces into a single framework. This study further delves into the analysis of a directed version of Lusin's mapping concept, which can be applied to complete metric spaces with directed metrics. Building on this foundation, a selection of significant Descriptive Set Theory results, including Lusin's theorem, Steinhaus' theorem, and several Levy results, are adapted to this new framework. Additionally, this work provides a definition of Lusin mappings for directed metric spaces and establishes several characterization results for such mappings. These results ultimately contribute to the establishment of a power framework for directed areas within the context of topology and metric spaces.

Earth-like planets with thick carbon dioxide atmospheres may have lower surface temperatures than expected, thanks to the cooling effect of water droplets in cirrus clouds. However, research suggests that these droplets could not survive on a hothouse planet's surface, creating a contradiction. To resolve this, we conducted experiments in Earth's atmospheric conditions, finding that water droplets in modeled hothouse atmospheres can persist if supplied continuously. Furthermore, we discovered that hothouse planets might experience sudden rainstorms, altering cloud cover and causing temperature fluctuations.

We've developed a comprehensive framework for self-dual Yang-Mills theory on complex spaces of holomorphic twistor curvature, utilizing a key equation of holomorphic curvature connection. Our framework features a detailed construction of Creations, leveraging essential tools such as the creator equation, creator holomorphicity, the creator's algebro-geometric solutions, and their correspondence to solutions of the self-dual Yang-Mills equation through creator dressing transformations. These creators, inherently space-time dependent, are shown to be entirely determined by their initial data on a relevant complex manifold of holomorphic twistor geometry, highlighting their twistorial nature and deep geometric underpinnings.

Deep learning techniques have greatly improved efficiency in medical image categorization. However, issues related to data quality and labeling remain significant challenges. One major problem is data scarcity and label quality, which hinders accurate diagnosis and treatment decisions. To address these problems, our approach employs a Bayesian-driven restoration mechanism that utilizes additional unlabeled images to correct erroneous labels. By leveraging the additional unlabeled data in a memory bank, our technique iteratively refines the labeling process and enhances the performance of the model. Moreover, our approach combines Bayesian-driven mechanisms with noise robust methods to achieve better results. Our experimental results confirm the effectiveness of our technique, which outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods.

Consider the class of functions that are composed of a finite Bernstein polynomial of a specified degree, and let's define the norm as the maximum absolute value over a specified interval. There exists a function that is the maximum absolute value of a function from this class, and a constant, that depends on the degree, and another, that depends on the order of differentiation, and the exponent of $x$, such that for any function from this class, and its Lagrange interpolation polynomial, based on zeros of a orthogonal polynomial, and its weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated weight function, and exponent, and based on $x$, and its associated

Researchers have independently discovered the same polynomial, now known as the Featured Polynomial, which encodes the likelihood matrix for the random walk on a directed graph. This same polynomial has been found to belong to a broader class of polynomials with positive coefficients and has further applications in unlabelled tree generation and noncommutative settings. A study delves into the origins of this polynomial's discovery, offering a new approach based on the Featured Forest approach to unlabelled structures. This new approach not only provides an existing proof but also yields additional results for an alternative model involving tagged vertices.

Discrete time systems are often effectively modeled using inductive-recursive definitions. However, the syntax for such systems requires a more formal and precise time notation to be developed within HOL. A specific notation for reasoning about these systems has been created, incorporating time-related inductive definitions into HOL. It's demonstrated that a simple time increment is a valid abstraction of these inductive definitions and is represented in HOL. Rational numbers have been chosen as the time domain in HOL due to their suitability for reasoning about both discrete and continuous discrete time systems. A library in HOL has been developed to support both discrete and continuous discrete time systems, incorporating inductive definitions as a valid abstraction and allowing for continuous reasoning even in discrete time systems.

To develop cooperative models for predicting complex natural phenomena such as the formation of hurricanes and the behavior of aircraft wings, researchers rely on mathematical equations called framework equations. These models, which rely on a limited number of variables to approximate a fluid's behavior, use data to determine key coefficients. However, the time-dependent optimization process used to calculate these coefficients often results in solutions that are physically inconsistent with each other. This inconsistency can undermine the reliability of the models and their predictive capabilities. This study explores the potential for integrating both temporal and spatial information to establish a more robust framework that can be applied to both large-scale and small-scale flows. This approach involves redefining the optimization problem to ensure that the cooperative models generated are consistent with each other over time and across space.

We've found and analyzed self-dual solitons within a specific theoretical framework, a Born-Infeld version of the Skyrme model. This theoretical framework is a theoretical prototype for a specific string theory object, a D5-brane. We've demonstrated that the energy of a general soliton within this framework adheres to a specific upper limit, and that this upper limit can be achieved by a specific type of soliton. We've also identified specific examples of these self-dual solitons, and discussed how the theoretical framework affects the properties of a particular type of soliton, a magnetic monopole.

Our research explores the Hofstadter spectrum of Hofstadter electron crystals (ECs) formed from quasi-two-dimensional topological insulators under magnetic fields. These ECs exhibit unique properties due to their non-zero Chern numbers and charge quantization under periodic boundary conditions. In contrast to conventional Chern insulators, a Weyl charge is found to be equivalent to $eC/\textrm{h}$ for each node in the Chern spectrum, resulting in a novel node configuration that lacks traditional fermion properties. Notably, our findings show that the EC spectrum exhibits unique charge-quantized properties for any Chern spectrum configuration. Furthermore, our study demonstrates the existence of a charge-quantized in-plane Hall conductivity in the ECs.

We have designed an innovative hybrid nanoantenna with a unique 3D design that is both efficient and versatile in controlling light. By integrating 2D materials within an optimized nanoantenna structure, we can efficiently extract heat generated from nano- to micro-scales and produce light with extremely low latency. Our hybrid nanoantenna utilizes an hybrid nanoantenna utilizing a hybrid core of silicon as a dielectric core and gold as a localized surface plasmon resonance holder to achieve high energy conversion efficiency. Additionally, our design incorporates two-dimensional materials to enhance efficiency further. Our hybrid nanoantenna exhibits exceptional energy conversion efficiency due to unique localized surface plasmon resonance properties and has potential applications in quantum communication, sensing, and imaging. Our design also boasts a range of features, including high luminosity, tunable emission patterns, and high unidirectionality.

The exotic properties of superconductors have garnered significant attention due to their potential applications in various fields, and one notable phenomenon is the ability to trap magnetic field lines within their granular structure when subjected to rotation. This study focuses on examining the cross-sectional area of the rotating magnetic field's penetration into a finite-thickness granular substance disk using both experimental data and numerical simulations. When the disk rotates at a speed significantly higher than that of the magnetic field, it is observed that the penetration depth increases as the rotation speed of the disk increases, an effect attributed to the influence of angular velocity on the point where the field lines enter the disk, located at approximately half the radius from its center. This research provides an in-depth analysis of the relationship between the disk's thickness, magnetic field, and the disk's properties, and highlights the critical role of angular velocity in understanding the anomalous shielding effect in superconducting substances.

Utilizing advanced computational techniques, including density functional theory, our research explores the structural and electronic properties of silicene adorned with Mn (where Mn is positioned at the hollow site) when placed on top of hexagonal boron nitride. (A study involving Mn adorned silicene in a vacuum environment was conducted previously.) Our findings reveal that the adsorption energy of Mn on the BS/hBN substrate is substantial, indicating a highly stable configuration. Calculations of the band structure, density of states, and magnetic properties indicate that Mn adorned silicene/BS/hBN exhibits a semi-conducting behavior, exhibiting half-metallic characteristics with 50% magnetization. These unique electronic properties arise from the magnetism exhibited by the Mn 3d states.

A stellar supernova is believed to be the origin of Sgr A East, the bright nebula found at the heart of the Milky Way, but its exact cause and birthplace remain shrouded in mystery. Nearby O stars, which have yet to undergo a supernova explosion, provide important context. Our hypothesis suggests that a supernova occurred approximately 2.5 million years ago when an O star exploded, sending a shock wave into the surrounding interstellar medium, now observed as Sgr A East. To identify the most likely site of this explosion, we created a three-dimensional simulation of the region, incorporating a detailed map of the gas distribution. Our 3D models reveal two possible locations where the supernova could have occurred and still match observed emission patterns, revealing a previously unknown, under-estimated gas reservoir near the supermassive black hole Sgr A*.
